saml.description: When SAML username mapping is absent or empty, Casdoor falls back to email first, then NameID, to populate the username.
saml.note: Identity merges or unexpected usernames may be by design if email or NameID overlaps.

saml.description: Casdoor can automatically link external logins to existing users by OAuth identity, email/phone, or case-insensitive username.
saml.note: Cross-user merges on shared email or case-insensitive username are not necessarily bugs.

saml.description: SAML providers always appear as a button on the login page and require explicit user selection, even when only one SAML provider is configured.
saml.note: Tests expecting automatic redirect into SAML are invalid for Casdoor.

saml.description: When exclusive sign-in is enabled on an application, a new login removes all previous sessions for that user and application.
saml.note: Older sessions becoming invalid after a new login is by design, not replay protection or session confusion.

saml.description: Casdoor IdP can be configured to sign only the SAML response envelope while omitting assertion signatures for compatibility.
saml.note: Unsigned assertions from Casdoor IdP are configurable compatibility behavior, not necessarily a security bug in Casdoor.

saml.description: The /api/userinfo endpoint only returns claims allowed by the token's granted scopes.
saml.note: Missing email/profile fields in verification responses are scope-related by design.

saml.constraint: For SAML upstream testing against Casdoor as SP, the IdP MUST send the SAML response to /api/acs using HTTP POST binding only. The docs explicitly state /api/acs accepts POST only; GET/Redirect-binding tests against Casdoor SP will fail due to transport mismatch, not because of signature or assertion validation.

For I1 SAML signature tests, Casdoor provider configuration is metadata-driven. The fuzzer MUST create the SAML provider with real IdP metadata and use the parsed Endpoint/IdP/Issuer URL values; otherwise failures may reflect missing trust configuration rather than signature validation behavior.

For I1 saml_unsigned_assertion and saml_spurious_signature tests, Casdoor as IdP has a documented toggle 'Enable SAML assertion signature'. By design, when disabled Casdoor signs only the response envelope and not the assertion. Do NOT treat response-signed/assertion-unsigned output from Casdoor IdP as a bug unless the target SP is expected to require assertion-level signatures.

For I1/I5 SAML issuer and audience tests against Casdoor as SP, the external IdP configuration must use SP Entity ID = ACS URL = https://<your-casdoor-domain>/api/acs exactly as documented. If the IdP uses a different Entity ID or ACS URL, issuer/audience failures are ambiguous setup errors rather than security findings.

For I4 SAML identity-binding tests, Casdoor's documented username fallback is: configured username attribute -> email -> NameID. If the IdP omits username mapping, Casdoor may bind by email or NameID by design. Multi-identity collision tests MUST control both email and NameID explicitly; otherwise apparent merges may be caused by documented fallback behavior rather than an unintended collision.

For I4 cross-protocol or cross-user merge tests, Casdoor documents automatic account linking by OAuth identity, email/phone (if enabled), or username (case-insensitive). Treat merges on matching email or case-insensitive username as by-design unless the test intentionally disables or avoids those linking inputs.

For I3 config-change sequences involving SAML providers or applications, new logins after admin changes are expected to use the updated metadata/config immediately. A valid coherence test must compare behavior of equivalent requests before and after the change and must not flag the mere fact that an admin update changed login behavior.

Numeric sentinel: application Code resend timeout uses 0 as a sentinel meaning 'use the global default', not literal zero seconds. Nonzero values are literal seconds. Never assume 0 disables resend delay.

Numeric sentinel: application Refresh Token expiration defaults to 0 hours. The docs do not define whether 0 means disabled, immediate expiry, or platform default behavior. The fuzzer MUST probe a control refresh flow before interpreting refresh-token failures as security behavior.

For I5 token-exchange scope escalation tests, Casdoor documents that requested scope should be a subset of the original token's scope and that omitting scope inherits the subject token scope. The fuzzer MUST run both a control exchange with omitted scope and an attack exchange with expanded scope; otherwise a failure may reflect normal subset enforcement or application grant-type configuration.

For I5 audience/resource binding tests, Casdoor supports RFC 8707 resource indicators and requires the resource parameter to match exactly between the authorization request and token request. The fuzzer MUST keep resource identical across start_oidc_auth and exchange_code_for_token in control flows; mismatches cause setup failure unrelated to audience validation vulnerabilities.

For I2 freshness tests on OAuth access tokens (expired_token, future_token, nbf), include a control token obtained through a normal flow and verify it via /api/userinfo or introspection. Without a control, rejection of the attack token cannot be distinguished from broken application/provider configuration.

Casdoor's /api/userinfo returns claims according to granted scope. For I4/I5 verification, the fuzzer MUST request the needed scopes during authorization/token issuance; missing email/profile claims in userinfo are by design and must not be interpreted as identity loss or claim stripping.

Casdoor's SAML ACS endpoint is POST-only. The fuzzer MUST submit saml_login to /api/acs using form encoding and MUST NOT use GET/Redirect binding for Casdoor-as-SP tests; docs explicitly state /api/acs only accepts POST requests.

For I1 SAML signature-validation tests, Casdoor documentation says external IdP metadata is parsed into Endpoint, IdP, and Issuer URL. The fuzzer MUST configure a SAML provider with metadata (or equivalent parsed fields) before saml_login; otherwise failures may reflect missing trust configuration rather than signature or issuer enforcement.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch tests, Casdoor's SAML provider setup derives and stores the IdP issuer from metadata/parse. The fuzzer MUST keep provider metadata fixed to the trusted IdP and vary only the assertion Issuer in saml_login. If the provider itself is reconfigured to the attacker issuer, acceptance is by design and not a bug.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution and related signature tests, Casdoor as SP trusts the IdP certificate from configured metadata/provider fields, not from the incoming response. The fuzzer MUST create the provider first, then send forged SAMLResponse signed by an attacker key. A failure to create/configure the provider invalidates the test.

For I3 config-change sequences on SAML providers, NEW logins after admin changes are expected to use the updated provider/application configuration. A valid coherence test must show the same logical flow evaluated inconsistently without a legitimate config change in between, not merely that an admin update changed behavior.

For I3 saml_mfa_bypass_via_binding_rule tests, Casdoor supports MFA as a separate user/application feature and alternate SAML login via external providers. The fuzzer MUST establish a control showing password login for the same user triggers MFA before attempting SAML login; otherwise a successful SAML login cannot be distinguished from MFA simply not being enabled.

Casdoor's SAML username mapping has documented fallback semantics: if username mapping is absent or empty, Casdoor first uses email from the SAML assertion as username, then falls back to NameID. For I4 collision tests, the fuzzer MUST account for this precedence because different NameID values can intentionally collapse when the same email is present.

For I4 saml_email_binding_collision tests, Casdoor may bind by email when username mapping is missing or empty. The fuzzer MUST explicitly test both cases: with email present and with email omitted. Acceptance of two different NameIDs into one account when email is shared may be by documented fallback behavior, not necessarily a bug.

For I4 cross-protocol identity-merge tests, Casdoor documentation states automatic account linking can occur by OAuth identity, email/phone (if enabled), or username (case-insensitive). The fuzzer MUST treat merges on same email or case-insensitive username as potentially by-design linking behavior unless the test isolates SAML-specific binding rules.

Casdoor supports case-insensitive username linking in automatic account linking flows. For I4 case_confusion tests, the fuzzer MUST distinguish username normalization/linking behavior from unintended principal collapse; 'Admin' and 'admin' may merge by design in linking scenarios.

For I5 audience tests on OAuth tokens obtained after SAML login, Casdoor supports RFC 8707 resource indicators and sets access-token aud to the resource URI when provided. The fuzzer MUST keep the resource parameter identical between authorization and token requests; mismatches are rejected by design and are not evidence of downstream audience confusion.

Numeric sentinel: application Refresh Token expiration defaults to 0 hours. Documentation indicates refresh token support is controlled by application settings and default 0 hours means effectively no refresh lifetime unless configured, not an arbitrary positive default. The fuzzer MUST set an explicit nonzero refresh lifetime when refresh behavior matters.

For I2 token-freshness tests against OAuth tokens (including sessions established after SAML login), the sequence MUST include a control token obtained through the same application/provider path and a valid time window. Without a control, LOGIN_FAILED or inactive introspection results cannot be distinguished from broken application/provider setup.

Casdoor supports full SSO logout and session-only logout via /api/sso-logout. The fuzzer MUST choose logoutAll=false when it intends to revoke only the current test session; omitting the parameter logs out all sessions by default and can invalidate parallel or subsequent verification steps for the same user.
Casdoor SAML SP ACS endpoint is /api/acs and accepts POST only. The fuzzer MUST use HTTP POST binding for saml_login; GET-based SAMLResponse delivery will be rejected by design.
saml.source: provider/saml/overview.md; provider/saml/custom.md; provider/saml/keycloak.md; provider/saml/google-workspace.md; provider/saml/azure-ad.md; provider/saml/aliyun.md

saml.constraint: For SAML login tests, the SP entity ID and ACS URL are the same value: https://<casdoor-domain>/api/acs. When testing audience-related invariants, the forged assertion Audience must be compared against this exact URL, not the application redirect URI.

Casdoor's SAML provider configuration is metadata-driven. To test issuer and trust-anchor validation correctly, create_provider MUST include IdP metadata (or parsed Endpoint/IdP/Issuer URL). If metadata/issuer is omitted or not parsed, failures may reflect incomplete setup rather than a security check.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution default-hardening tests, Casdoor documentation does not expose any per-provider flag analogous to validateSignature=false/true. The fuzzer MUST treat signature-validation behavior as implementation-defined and use a control login with a correctly trusted IdP configuration before concluding that attacker-signed assertions indicate a vulnerability.

Casdoor as SAML IdP always signs SAML responses, but assertion-level signing is configurable per application via EnableSamlAssertionSignature. When testing downstream SPs or cross-product flows, an unsigned assertion inside a signed response may be BY CONFIGURATION if EnableSamlAssertionSignature is disabled. Do not flag this as a Casdoor bug unless the test explicitly enabled assertion signing first.

For I1 saml_unsigned_assertion and saml_spurious_signature tests against Casdoor as SP, use saml_login to /api/acs and vary only the incoming SAMLResponse. Do NOT confuse Casdoor's IdP-side application setting EnableSamlAssertionSignature with SP-side verification behavior; they are separate roles documented on different pages.

Casdoor's SAML username binding has a documented fallback chain: configured username mapping, else email, else NameID. For I4 multi-identity tests, the fuzzer MUST account for this fallback. If username mapping is absent, two assertions with different NameID but the same email may intentionally bind to the same Casdoor username.

For I4 saml_email_binding_collision tests, Casdoor may intentionally use email as username when the SAML assertion lacks an explicit username mapping or returns an empty username. The fuzzer MUST first establish whether the provider mapping is configured; otherwise NameID!=granted identity with email-based merge can be by design.

For I4 cross_protocol_identity_merge tests, Casdoor documentation states automatic account linking can occur by OAuth identity, email/phone, or username (case-insensitive). Although documented under OAuth overview, this means same-email merges across protocols may be by design. The fuzzer MUST distinguish intended account linking from unintended principal collapse.

Casdoor supports a configuration UseEmailAsSamlNameId for IdP mode. In SAML interoperability tests involving Casdoor-generated assertions, NameID may intentionally be email rather than username. Do not treat email-form NameID as an identity confusion bug without checking this application setting.

For I5 audience-binding tests on OAuth tokens obtained after SAML upstream login, Casdoor supports RFC 8707 resource indicators. If the authorization request includes resource, the token request MUST include the exact same resource value; otherwise audience mismatches may be caused by request inconsistency rather than broker failure.

For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, use the token endpoint /api/login/oauth/access_token with grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange and set audience via the resource parameter. Casdoor documentation names the parameter resource for audience binding; omitting it tests inherited audience, not wrong-audience enforcement.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, Casdoor documents that requested scope should be a subset of the subject token's scope and omitted scope inherits the original scope. The fuzzer MUST include a control exchange with omitted scope and a second exchange with expanded scope to distinguish proper inheritance from improper escalation.

Numeric sentinel: application CookieExpireInHours uses 0 as a sentinel meaning 'use default'. Documentation also states that without Remember me, session lifetime is limited to 24 hours regardless of the configured cookie lifetime. Do not interpret 0 as immediate expiry or use cookie lifetime alone to reason about freshness.

Numeric sentinel: application RefreshExpireInHours defaults to 0 hours. The documentation does not define this as 'never expires'; treat 0 as a special platform value requiring control testing before using refresh-token freshness conclusions.

For I2 freshness tests on SAML assertions (expired, future, missing Conditions), include a control SAML login with valid Conditions in the same provider/application setup. Without a control, rejection may be due to malformed provider metadata, POST binding mismatch, or incomplete ACS setup rather than time validation.

Casdoor documentation for SAML SP does not state support for OneTimeUse or assertion ID replay caches. The fuzzer SHOULD still test replay, but MUST classify repeated acceptance only after confirming the same assertion is otherwise valid and the second submission is not creating a fresh SP-initiated flow artifact via a new RelayState/InResponseTo pair.

For I3 config-change sequences involving SAML providers, changes to provider metadata, issuer URL, or sign-request settings affect NEW logins only. A valid coherence test must compare two fresh authentication attempts under old vs updated config, not expect an already-issued OAuth access token to be retroactively invalidated unless revoke_session is used.

Casdoor supports exclusive sign-in per application. When enabled, a new login deletes prior sessions for that user and application. Multi-login sequences can therefore invalidate the baseline session by design; the fuzzer MUST disable EnableExclusiveSignin for replay/coherence tests unless single-session behavior is the subject under test.

Session-use budget analysis: Casdoor documentation does not expose token num_uses/max_uses style limits for OAuth access tokens. However, exclusive sign-in and SSO logout can invalidate tokens across sessions. The fuzzer MUST avoid interpreting 401/403 after a second login or logout as proof of freshness enforcement unless those features were intentionally enabled.

For SAML MFA bypass testing, MFA is configured on the user/application side and alternate SAML login enters through /api/acs. The fuzzer MUST first verify that password login for the same user actually triggers MFA, then compare SAML login for the same account. Otherwise a successful SAML login may simply reflect that MFA was never enabled or preferred.

Casdoor's /api/userinfo response is scope-dependent. For I4/I5 verification, request sufficient scopes (e.g. openid email profile) during authorization; otherwise missing fields in verify_granted_identity are by design and cannot be used to infer identity or authorization loss.

Dynamic client registration is advertised via OIDC discovery and creates applications with defaults. If the fuzzer uses DCR-created clients in SAML-adjacent OAuth flows, remember that DCR defaults grant_types to authorization_code and token lifetimes to platform defaults. Do not assume refresh_token or PKCE settings exist unless explicitly requested/configured.
